title: Embedded Systems & Microcontrollers
blurb: Microcontrollers, GPIO, sensors, timers, interrupts, firmware architecture, device communication, and Python-based simulation.
description: Learn embedded-system thinking with Python and MicroPython-style patterns while keeping browser practice safe and runnable.

lessons.title: Microcontrollers & the embedded mindset
objectives: Reason about memory, timing, power, and hardware constraints
Explain how microcontroller changes the behavior, result, or engineering decision in a concrete example
Connect microcontroller with flash and predict what changes when one assumption changes
Verify the idea with a normal case and an important edge, failure, or scale case
lessons.explanation: A microcontroller combines a CPU, flash, RAM, timers, communication peripherals, and GPIO on one device, usually under tighter memory, power, timing, and cost constraints than a desktop computer. Firmware often interacts directly with hardware registers or device drivers and may need predictable timing.
commonMistakes: Designing as if the device has desktop-class memory, power, storage, and timing.
lessons.explain: A microcontroller combines a CPU, flash, RAM, timers, communication peripherals, and GPIO on one device, usually under tighter memory, power, timing, and cost constraints than a desktop computer. Firmware often interacts directly with hardware registers or device drivers and may need predictable timing.

lessons.title: GPIO: digital inputs & outputs
lessons.explanation: GPIO pins can be configured as digital inputs or outputs. Inputs can float unless pull-up or pull-down resistors establish a known default level.
examples:
samples = [1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1]
stable = samples[-3:]
pressed = stable == [0, 0, 0]
print("pressed:", pressed)
commonMistakes: Reading a button or digital input without a defined pull-up/pull-down or debounce strategy, causing floating or repeated transitions to look like real events.
lessons.explain: GPIO pins can be configured as digital inputs or outputs. Inputs can float unless pull-up or pull-down resistors establish a known default level.

lessons.title: Timers, delays & interrupts
lessons.explanation: Timers provide hardware-based time measurement so firmware does not have to waste CPU cycles in long busy-wait loops. Interrupts let hardware signal that an event needs attention, but interrupt handlers should remain short because they can delay other time-sensitive work.
examples:
import asyncio

async def sample_sensor():
    for tick in range(3):
        print("sample", tick)
        await asyncio.sleep(0)

asyncio.run(sample_sensor())
commonMistakes: Using long blocking delays inside the main control loop, which prevents the device from responding to other events on time.
lessons.explain: Timers provide hardware-based time measurement so firmware does not have to waste CPU cycles in long busy-wait loops. Interrupts let hardware signal that an event needs attention, but interrupt handlers should remain short because they can delay other time-sensitive work.

lessons.title: ADC, PWM & analog signals
lessons.explanation: An ADC converts an analog voltage into a discrete digital number. Resolution determines how many distinct codes are available, while sampling rate determines how often the signal is measured.
examples:
raw = 2530
max_adc = 4095
volts = raw * (3.3 / max_adc)
duty = round(raw / max_adc * 100, 1)
print(volts, duty)
commonMistakes: Treating ADC readings and PWM output as perfectly exact analog values.
lessons.explain: An ADC converts an analog voltage into a discrete digital number. Resolution determines how many distinct codes are available, while sampling rate determines how often the signal is measured.

lessons.title: UART, I²C & SPI communication
objectives: Design a small device communication layer
lessons.explanation: UART, I²C, and SPI solve different communication needs. UART is asynchronous point-to-point serial communication.
commonMistakes: Mixing UART/I2C/SPI details directly into application logic.
lessons.explain: UART, I²C, and SPI solve different communication needs. UART is asynchronous point-to-point serial communication.

lessons.title: Sensors, actuators & device drivers
lessons.explanation: A device driver translates application-level intent into the register operations or bus messages a specific sensor or actuator expects. Sensors often require calibration, scaling, unit conversion, and plausibility checks before raw readings become useful data.
commonMistakes: Using raw sensor values as trustworthy application data without calibration, unit conversion, range checks, timeout handling, or a defined safe response to device failure.
lessons.explain: A device driver translates application-level intent into the register operations or bus messages a specific sensor or actuator expects. Sensors often require calibration, scaling, unit conversion, and plausibility checks before raw readings become useful data.

lessons.title: Firmware architecture & state machines
lessons.explanation: A state machine makes firmware behavior explicit by listing valid states, the events that cause transitions, and the actions performed on entry or transition. This is often safer than a collection of loosely related flags.
examples:
from enum import Enum
class State(Enum):
    IDLE = "idle"
    RUNNING = "running"
    FAULT = "fault"

state = State.IDLE
temperature = 82
state = State.FAULT if temperature > 70 else State.RUNNING
print(state.value)
commonMistakes: Representing modes with scattered booleans and implicit rules instead of explicit states and transitions, making impossible states and unsafe transitions hard to detect.
lessons.explain: A state machine makes firmware behavior explicit by listing valid states, the events that cause transitions, and the actions performed on entry or transition. This is often safer than a collection of loosely related flags.

lessons.title: Embedded testing & debugging
lessons.explanation: Embedded testing combines ordinary unit tests with hardware-aware techniques. Logic can often be tested on a host computer or simulator, while integration tests exercise real peripherals.
examples:
def should_start(temp, interlock):
    return interlock and temp < 70

assert should_start(30, True)
assert not should_start(80, True)
print("logic tests passed")
commonMistakes: Testing only on physical hardware or only on the happy path.
lessons.explain: Embedded testing combines ordinary unit tests with hardware-aware techniques. Logic can often be tested on a host computer or simulator, while integration tests exercise real peripherals.

exercises.title: Resource-budget check
exercises.prompt: A device has 64 KB of RAM. Model a sensor buffer that stores 600 samples with 16 bytes per sample plus 8 KB for the rest of the program. Calculate the memory used, report whether it fits, and explain what you would change if the buffer exceeded the budget.

exercises.title: Debounced button press
exercises.prompt: Given a time-ordered sequence of noisy 0/1 button readings, write logic that reports one press only after the input has stayed stable for the required debounce interval. Demonstrate a bouncing press and a clean press.

exercises.title: Non-blocking periodic tasks
exercises.prompt: Simulate an embedded main loop where an LED toggles every 500 ms while a sensor is checked every 200 ms. Do not use a long blocking sleep; show from the timestamps that both periodic behaviors continue to run.

exercises.title: ADC reading to voltage
exercises.prompt: For a 12-bit ADC with a 3.3 V reference, convert raw readings such as 0, 2048, and 4095 into voltage. Clamp or reject readings outside the valid range and explain the effect of ADC resolution.

exercises.title: PWM actuator controller
exercises.prompt: Model a PWM-controlled fan or LED that maps a 0–100% command to duty cycle. Validate invalid commands and show what output duty cycle is produced for low, medium, and maximum requests.

exercises.title: Choose the device bus
exercises.prompt: A controller must connect a debug console, several addressed sensors on two shared wires, and one high-speed local display. Decide which of UART, I2C, or SPI fits each connection and justify the wiring, addressing, and speed trade-off.

exercises.title: Calibrated sensor driver
exercises.prompt: Create a driver-style function that turns a raw sensor count into engineering units using calibration values. Detect an impossible reading or timeout and return an explicit error/fault instead of silently using bad data.

exercises.title: Controller state machine
exercises.prompt: Model IDLE, ARMED, and ALARM states. Define the events that allow each transition, reject an invalid transition, and print the state after a normal sequence and a fault sequence.

exercises.title: Watchdog-safe fault response
exercises.prompt: Simulate a control loop with a heartbeat/watchdog deadline. If the heartbeat is not updated in time, move the controller to a safe fault state and show that unsafe outputs are disabled.

exercises.title: Embedded fault-injection test
exercises.prompt: Write tests for a hardware-independent decision function by injecting a normal sensor value, an out-of-range value, and a timeout/failure. Show the expected safe behavior for each case.

exercises.title: Bounded telemetry buffer
exercises.prompt: Model a fixed-capacity telemetry/log buffer for a memory-constrained device. When the buffer fills, apply a defined policy such as dropping the oldest record, and prove the buffer never grows beyond its limit.

exercises.title: Integrated device loop
exercises.prompt: Build a small simulation combining a debounced input, periodic sensor sampling, a state-machine decision, and an actuator output. Demonstrate one normal operating sequence and one sensor/input fault without blocking the whole loop.

projects.title: Smart environmental monitor
projects.description: Build a Python simulation for temperature/light sensing, non-blocking updates, alarms, and structured logging.
requirements: Use at least two simulated sensor inputs
Add a state or fault model

projects.title: Event-driven reaction timer
projects.description: Model timers, input debouncing, and state transitions to build a precise reaction-timer simulation.

projects.title: Multi-sensor safety controller
projects.description: Create a fault-tolerant Python controller with driver boundaries, state machines, safe outputs, and tests.
requirements: Add fault handling and safe outputs

capstone.title: Production-style embedded controller simulation
capstone.description: Design a Python controller for a small device with multiple sensors and outputs, non-blocking timing, explicit fault handling, communication boundaries, and testable logic.
deliverables: At least two sensors and two outputs
Unit tests and a hardware/simulation test plan

careerApplications: Role-specific company use in firmware, IoT, robotics, automotive, devices, and hardware-software integration.

quiz.q: What best describes a microcontroller?
options: A CPU, memory, and peripherals integrated for dedicated control tasks
A desktop operating system running in the cloud

quiz.q: Why do RAM, flash, power, and timing limits matter in embedded design?
options: They determine whether the software can fit and meet the device requirements
They matter only after the product ships
They affect only the display color

quiz.q: Which statement about flash and RAM is generally correct for a microcontroller?
options: Flash is typically non-volatile program/storage memory; RAM is volatile working memory
RAM is non-volatile and flash is always faster working memory
They are exactly the same resource

quiz.q: What is a pull-up or pull-down used for on a digital input?
options: To give the input a defined default level instead of leaving it floating
To convert analog voltage into a digital number

quiz.q: Why is button debouncing needed?
options: One physical press can create several rapid electrical transitions
Buttons can only be read through SPI

quiz.q: What does edge detection look for?
options: A transition from one digital state to another
Only how long the signal stays high

quiz.q: What is the main risk of a long blocking delay in a control loop?
options: Other time-sensitive work cannot run while the code is blocked
It makes interrupts impossible on every platform

quiz.q: In embedded software, interrupt latency is the time between:
options: An event occurring and the system beginning the required response
Two UART characters regardless of software

quiz.q: Why use non-blocking timer/event logic?
options: To let multiple time-dependent tasks make progress without freezing the whole loop

quiz.q: What does an ADC do?
options: Converts an analog input level into a digital numeric reading

quiz.q: Increasing ADC resolution primarily gives you:
options: More discrete numeric levels across the input range

quiz.q: A 25% PWM duty cycle means the signal is active for approximately:
options: One quarter of each PWM period
One quarter of the program lifetime

quiz.q: Which bus is commonly chosen for several addressed peripherals sharing two signal wires?
What is a common characteristic of SPI?
options: High-speed synchronous transfers using separate clock/data lines and chip-select signals
Built-in device addressing over only two wires for every device
It requires no clock or framing agreement
It is only for internet routing

quiz.q: UART is commonly used as:
options: A simple asynchronous serial link such as a debug console or point-to-point device connection

quiz.q: Why put sensor/bus details behind a device driver boundary?
options: Application logic can use meaningful operations without depending on raw protocol details
It removes the need for any error handling
It guarantees every sensor is accurate
It prevents the device from using memory

quiz.q: What is calibration used for?
options: Mapping raw device readings to meaningful, corrected units or behavior

quiz.q: What should application code do with an impossible sensor reading or timeout?
options: Handle it explicitly according to the device safety/error policy
Silently treat it as a valid normal reading
Always reboot without recording the cause
Convert it to a random value

quiz.q: Why is an explicit state machine useful in firmware?
options: It makes allowed operating modes and transitions clear and testable
It automatically chooses the hardware bus

quiz.q: What is a watchdog intended to detect?
options: Software that has stopped making expected progress

quiz.q: Deterministic control logic aims to make behavior:
options: Predictable for a given state/input and timing assumptions

quiz.q: What design choice makes embedded logic easier to unit test on a normal computer?
options: Separate pure decision/state logic from hardware I/O
Put every hardware call directly inside every condition
Use only physical hardware for every test

quiz.q: What is fault injection?
options: Deliberately simulating failures such as timeouts or bad readings to verify the response

quiz.q: A useful embedded debug log should help you reconstruct:
options: Relevant time/event/state changes around the failure
